sentences.text: Desmatosuchus is an extinct genus of archosaur that is classified as a reptile.
This large quadrupedal reptile measured between 4.5 and over 5 meters in length and weighed approximately 280 to 300 kilograms.
Like many relatives, it had bony plates covering its back, tail, and parts of its lower body.
Unlike other aetosaurs, Desmatosuchus had two rows of spines running along the sides of its back.
The largest spines, located over the shoulders, measured 45 centimeters in length.

The lateral scutes had well-developed spine-like processes that pointed out laterally and dorso-posteriorly, while the front spine was much larger, measuring around 28 centimeters in length, and was recurved.
These spines likely provided additional protection against predators.
Desmatosuchus is unique among aetosaurs because its species are the only known ones to lack teeth on their premaxillae.
It was featured in the Discovery Channel documentary When Dinosaurs Roamed America, where it was shown driving away a Coelophysis and later the predator Rutiodon.
It also appeared in an episode of the miniseries Animal Armageddon, where it was hunted by Staurikosaurus, one of the earliest dinosaurs, in a eventual extinction event.
The genus Desmatosuchus was first described by Case in 1920.
There are 14 recorded fossil occurrences of Desmatosuchus.
Desmatosuchus likely fed by digging up soft vegetation, indicated by its shovel-like snout and blunt teeth.
It possessed a shovel-shaped snout and weak teeth, suggesting it fed by pulling off soft plants.
Some researchers suggest Desmatosuchus may have been omnivorous or even an insectivore, though the general consensus remains that it was herbivorous.
The armor and spikes were the only means of defense Desmatosuchus had against predators.
Fossil evidence shows that Postosuchus preyed on Desmatosuchus, as Desmatosuchus bones have been found among Postosuchus skeletons.
Variation in the size of the second most anterior spike may indicate sexual dimorphism or serve as a form of sexual display.
Its parent group is Desmatosuchini.
It belongs to the family Stagonolepididae.
The type species is Desmatosuchus spurensis.
Two species are currently accepted as valid for Desmatosuchus: D. spurensis and D. smalli, the latter named after Brian J. Small.
Three species are considered valid: D. haplocerus, D. spurensis, and D. smalli.
D. chamaensis is considered a distinct genus, but there is controversy regarding whether it should be referred to the genera Heliocanthus or Rioarribasuchus.
Desmatosuchus lived during the Late Triassic, specifically from the Carnian to the Norian stages.
It lived from the Carnian to the Norian stages, between 237 and 205.7 million years ago.
Fossils of Desmatosuchus have been found in North America and potentially in India during the Late Triassic.
Desmatosuchus lived during the Triassic period in Texas.
